title: GRAFT: Gradient Routing Localizes and Removes Unintended Behaviors in RL
authors: Jake Ward and Shawn Hu (equal contribution, order randomised), Aria Wong, Nathan Hu, Bryce Woodworth, Alexander Matt Turner, Alex Cloud
venue: arXiv preprint (the code README says NeurIPS 2026)
date: 12 October 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version as of 26 October 2026); Anthropic Alignment Science Blog post 19 October 2026

code.title: jnward/GRAFT
code.note: The GRPO trainer with GRAFT and every baseline, the environments, monitors and sweeps, the Qwen3-32B SFT pipeline, the figure scripts and a 7.6 MB bundle of figure inputs (per-seed evaluations and training logs) that this page replays (MIT, vLLM patches Apache-2.0; read at commit b0767d1c on 26 October 2026). Training needs H200-class GPUs

takeaway: Routing the gradients of monitor-flagged RL samples into a separate adapter that is deleted after training, instead of penalising them, kept Qwen3-8B on Countdown-Code from learning the undetected hack a penalty taught (1.6% hacking after deletion against 26%) at a slightly lower solve rate; shown with keyword-style monitors on models up to 8B (RL) and one 32B SFT run.
verdict: Believe the Countdown result: the released per-seed data reproduce Figure 2 exactly, and the contrast with the penalty (which moved the model to an undetected hack on 26% of answers) is large next to seed noise. Treat the generality as open: the environments and monitors were chosen so that penalties fail, baselines have three seeds and the 32B run one, GRAFT usually solves fewer tasks than the penalty does, and the mechanism is not pinned down; in our toy, whose adapters share nothing, the deployed model still used an undetected hack on about a third of its answers.

headline.k: Qwen3-8B on Countdown-Code after training: GRAFT with the forget adapter deleted against a reward penalty on what the monitor flags, which taught an undetected hack (base model 4.7%)

headline.k: Qwen3-32B fine-tuned on Terminal Wrench trajectories, half of them hacks: hacking under a hack-elicitation prompt, GRAFT against filtering out every hack (both about 44% correct)
headline.d: one seed per method; without the prompt every method but two hacks under about 5%
